title: Akash Deep takes five as New Zealand make 356, but India lose two early in Christchurch
dek: Tom Blundell's 89 held up India on day two of the second Test. Matt Henry bowled Yashasvi Jaiswal for a duck in the first over of India's reply.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Akash Deep took five wickets for 99 as New Zealand were bowled out for 356 on the second day of the second Test at Hagley Oval in Christchurch, but India made a shaky start to their reply, losing Yashasvi Jaiswal and Devdutt Padikkal inside eight overs.

At about 7:45 am IST, during the second session, India were 33 for two, 323 runs behind, with K.L. Rahul on 9 and captain Shubman Gill yet to score. Jaiswal was bowled by Matt Henry for a duck in the first over, and Padikkal made a brisk 21 off 20 balls before he edged Kyle Jamieson to wicketkeeper Tom Blundell.

## How New Zealand's innings ended

New Zealand resumed on 246 for five and added 110 more. India struck early when Anshul Kamboj had Glenn Phillips caught behind without adding to his overnight 36. Akash Deep then took a return catch to remove Nathan Smith for 26 and dismissed Jamieson for 19.

Blundell, who began the day on 53, batted for 211 balls for his 89, with 10 fours, before he was caught on the fine-leg boundary by Akash Deep off debutant Gurnoor Brar shortly after lunch. Henry hit four fours in a quick 19 before he was the last man out, in the 117th over. Tom Latham had made 59 on the first day.

Akash Deep finished with 5 for 99 from 31.3 overs. Brar, playing his first Test in place of Prasidh Krishna, took 2 for 78 and Kamboj 2 for 79. Washington Sundar took one wicket, while Jasprit Bumrah went wicketless, conceding 49 runs from 26 overs by the last available count.

## The series so far

The first Test in Wellington was drawn. New Zealand made 368 in their first innings, with Henry Nicholls carrying his bat for an unbeaten 175, and India replied with 720 for nine declared, the highest total in any Test in New Zealand. Daryl Mitchell and Phillips then batted through most of the last two sessions, and New Zealand finished on 239 for five, 113 runs behind. Both teams took four points in the World Test Championship. That leaves the two-match series level, so a result in Christchurch would decide it.

Gill won the toss on Friday and chose to bowl. India's batting depth was the strength of their Wellington performance, when Rahul made 136, Gill 98 and Rishabh Pant 128.

## India's attack

India went in with a pace-heavy attack again, as they had in Wellington, where Gill had said before the series that India would play four fast bowlers. Brar replaced Prasidh Krishna, the only change, while New Zealand named an unchanged side. Bumrah, who took four for 92 in New Zealand's first innings in Wellington, kept the scoring down but could not break through on the second morning, and it was Akash Deep who did most of the damage, taking three of the five wickets to fall on day two.

## What happens next

Play is scheduled to end at 6 pm local time, 10:30 am IST. The third day starts at 3:30 am IST on Sunday. Details in this report are from the live scorecard and may change as play goes on.
